title: Requirements Analysis and Data Modeling knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes “Requirements Analysis and Data Modeling”?
options: It is a frontend styling feature and does not involve database behavior.
It guarantees correct output regardless of schema, permissions, or release version.
It is best handled by removing constraints and skipping error checks.

Requirements Analysis and Data Modeling is best learned by defining the expected behavior, inspecting a small MySQL example, and checking how the choice affects correctness, security, or operations. Keep assumptions explicit and validate version-sensitive details against the official manual.

questions.prompt: Which practice best applies “Requirements Analysis and Data Modeling” safely?
options: Concatenate untrusted input into SQL text and grant administrator privileges to every application user.
Judge success only by whether the statement returns any rows, without checking expected behavior or edge cases.
Apply Requirements Analysis and Data Modeling to a synthetic MySQL lab scenario, write down the expected outcome, and specify how you will verify it safely.
Skip testing, assume every SQL engine behaves identically, and apply the change directly to production.

questions.prompt: Before relying on an example for “Requirements Analysis and Data Modeling”, what should be verified?

Run a broad production change before checking the current state.
Ignore version notes and infer behavior from an unrelated database engine.
